title: Woody Herman's Texas tour and Jake Hanna
summary: Woody hired Jake Hanna to avoid Jim Crow in Texas, then phoned in surprise at integrated hotels.

story.theme_name: Race and segregation in the jazz life
story.community_name: Segregation on the road and the bandstand

blocks.x: Just like Woody Herman. Well, I played on the big bands, too, see. And I'm trying to -- let's see, I think it was -- about '65, when he went down -- no, 60-something, when Jake Hannah joined the band.
Yeah.
Well, they left and went to Brownsville, Texas.
Oh?
They were going to Brownsville, Texas. That's when Woody got Jake Hannah, because he figured that there was going to be a lot of Jim Crow, you know.
Yeah.
And they were on their way to Houston, Texas.
Yeah.
So he told me, he'd say he didn't want me to feel bad about it.
Yeah.
And --
He figured you things would be ticklish.
Yeah, kind of ticklish. I told him, no, I wasn't going to be ticklish about it. But that's the way -- if you think it's going to be like that, okay. Which at that time was --
Yeah.
He hadn't been down there.
Yeah.

And so, they left and went to Houston first, and by the time they got to Houston, he called me long distance. Nat Pierce called me. He said, 'Man, Woody want to talk to you.' I said, 'Yeah? What's the matter now?' He said, 'He just wants to tell you something that happened.' And so he put him on the phone. And first thing he said, 'Hey, Gus Dick -- now, wait, he got that from a florist we passed by. It was a name, see, and it was another name, Cockburn was the name. And so I would call him Woody Cockburn, one of those things. I say, 'Yeah, Woody Cockburn, what are you saying?' He said, 'You're not going to believe this.' I said, 'Now what's wrong?' He said, 'I get here at the Rice Hotel, in Houston, and my rooms are not ready. And I send for the manager, and the manager came out.' And he said, 'Guess what,' and I said, 'What?' He say, 'The manager is a black man here.' I said, 'Yeah?' I said, 'Well, what's wrong with that?' He said, 'Nothing, but he rang for the bellboy and when the bellboy came up, it's a white boy.'
And I told him about my rooms, and he went right on and got my rooms for me. He said, 'things have really changed down here.'
(Laughter.)
I said, 'Well, can you believe that? I don't believe that.' And he went down to Brownsville, Texas, and he told that things had changed down there. So I said, 'Well, that's the way it is.'
He moved in haste.
Yes, sir. You never know until-you get there. Which I didn't know, either, see. But everything turned out all right.
Yeah.
And I made a lot of dates with him since then, see.
Yeah.
But that's the way it was.
Yeah.
So I never had any trouble.
No, no, yeah. That's -- some guys are hotheaded.
Yeah.
And they're going to jump to it right away before maybe it's necessary, and --
